## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components with fused updates can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p drops from 12.736 at N=4000 (past the L1d spill at 897, within L2) to 8.369 at N=65000 (just past the L2 spill at 57456), then holds flat at 8.351 through N=262000 before a slight rise to 8.716–8.779 at N≥1M. The small-N penalty is overhead amortization, not cache capacity — the L2→DRAM spill produces no knee, only modest improvement as fixed costs dilute. Raising death rate lifts the floor uniformly without reshaping the curve: q=0.05 stabilizes at ~9.3 ns/p (rising to ~10.3 at large N), q=0.25 at ~13.4–13.5 ns/p. Death rate raises the floor; it does not introduce cache-dependent structure.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.74 GB/s at N=262000, q=0.01 — 34.7% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. The algo is compute/overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: achieved bandwidth is flat across N past the small-N regime (8.3–8.7 GB/s at q=0.01 for N≥65000), never climbing toward the ceiling as N grows. Death rate degrades it monotonically — q=0.05 peaks at 7.85 GB/s (31.1%), q=0.25 at 5.44 GB/s (21.6%). The transition from overhead-bound to steady-state occurs by N=65000; the transition to churn-bound occurs between q=0.05 and q=0.25. PMC data is unavailable, so cycle attribution cannot confirm the bottleneck.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized component-wise within one particle, not across particles. `ldur q16` loads 16 bytes of a particle's data, `ext.16b v18, v16, v17, #0xc` rearranges lanes, and `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` perform 4-lane arithmetic on that particle's components. An indexed load `ld1.s { v17 }[1], [x11]` gathers a single component into one vector lane, followed by `fmul.2s`/`fadd.2s` for the remaining pair. The 5 `strb` instructions are byte-granular mask writes — one per particle marking alive/dead. This component-wise scheme with gather (`ld1.s`) and byte stores (`strb`) explains the 35% ceiling: indexed loads and byte-granular writes cannot stream, and the per-particle `fmul`/`fadd` chains plus 6 `bl` calls (spawn, splat, fill) make the loop compute-heavy rather than memory-limited.

## Verdict
Refuted — peak achieved bandwidth never exceeds 8.74 GB/s (34.7% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at q=0.01, N=262000, and the component-wise vectorization with `ld1.s` gather and `strb` byte stores cannot stream. At q=0.25 the algo falls to 5.44 GB/s (21.6% of ceiling). The hypothesis that autovec approaches the streaming ceiling fails even in the lowest-churn regime.
